text:
Jules: hey @support I'm getting 401 (invalid_api_key) for service-x after yesterday's key rotation. New key works from my home laptop but fails from the office network behind our proxy. curl just returns 401 invalid_api_key, no other clues. Anyone seen org-level IP allowlist cause this?

Priya: can you paste the curl you ran (redact the key) and the raw response body if possible? helps a lot.

Jules: sure -- redacted but same shape:
```
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_KEY\" \n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n```
response body: `{"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"key restricted: source_ip not allowed","error_id":"err_01abc"}`

SupportBot: Automated lookup: err_01abc -> restriction_type=ip_allowlist, org_policy=restrict_new_keys, created_by=console-api (Mar 30).

Priya: ah that message is explicit — key was rejected because the incoming source IP isn't in the key's allowed sources. Two quick asks: 1) can you confirm the public IP the office egress shows (curl to https://ifconfig.co) and 2) does the Console show any \"Allowed sources\" on that key?

Jules: office egress shows `203.0.113.45` from ifconfig.co. Console for new key shows Allowed sources: `10.0.0.0/8` (company internal) and `198.51.100.17` (dev laptop) — looks like the proxy masks office IP so the public IP isn't listed.

ana_ops: I rolled out a tightened org policy yesterday that defaults newly rotated keys to an IP allowlist for safety (policy: restrict_new_keys=true). It only prepopulates a couple developer IPs; if users don't add the org egress IPs you'll hit this 401. I can add the office egress IP to the key or relax the policy for this key.

Priya: for immediate workaround either: 1) add `203.0.113.45` into Allowed sources for that key (Console -> Keys -> Edit Allowed sources) or 2) create a new key and leave Allowed sources blank (no restrictions). If you need a scoped key instead, make sure the scope includes `inference:generate` and policy won't change the allowlist.

Jules: can you add `203.0.113.45` to the key? would prefer not to create a new key mid-day.

ana_ops: added `203.0.113.45` to allowed sources for key id `k_9xyz`. Also linked the change to ticket #12345. Try again.

Jules: retrying now... curl returns 200 and tokens streaming — working! :tada: Thanks everyone.

SupportBot: Ticket #12345 updated: resolution=added_office_egress_ip, closure_pending_customer_confirm.
